resources.string: A simple visual guide, right over your screen.
Allow the overlay, then start a screen-sharing session.
Look for the cyan marker on a colored ring. You can still tap and swipe through it.
Screen sharing was cancelled. Tap Start when you are ready.
Display over other apps is required. Enable it in Settings, then tap Start.
Screen capture could not start. Check overlay permission, then try a new session.
Screen capture was interrupted. Tap Start to try again.
The display size or orientation changed. Tap Start for a new session with aligned guidance.
Share the entire screen so the marker can line up. Tap Start and choose the entire screen.
Screen capture has stopped. No frames are being analyzed.
Android ended screen sharing. Tap Start to begin a new session.
Screen frames are analyzed on this device, never saved or uploaded. Sharing covers your entire screen; stop before opening private content.

1. Tap Start and approve Android’s screen-sharing prompt.

2. Open the practice screen or switch to your target app. A cyan marker appears when a colored ring is detected.

3. Stop from this app, the notification, or Android’s sharing controls.
Detection and automatic throws are experimental. Rings can be missed or mistaken for other objects, and swipes can miss. Throw grades and catches are not predicted.
Analyzing your screen on this device. Tap to open controls.
Hold the ball to reveal its ring, then swipe toward it. For Auto: start capture, Set ball, then arm. Scoring checks screen position and movement timing, not game physics.
Practice ball and target. Hold the ball to reveal the shrinking ring, then drag upward toward it.
Hold the ball, then swipe in 150–600 ms
Android could not open overlay settings. Enable “Display over other apps” in the app’s system settings.

Optional automatic swipes in Pokémon GO or the visible practice encounter, only after you calibrate a ball position and turn Auto on. Calibration is separate for game and practice. The service checks the focused app package and window bounds; it does not read or store UI text. Stop ends capture and disables future throws.
Enable Throw Assistant gestures in Android Accessibility settings.
Gesture permission enabled — waiting for Android to connect the service
Gesture service off — overlay guidance still works

Enable “Throw Assistant gestures” in Accessibility settings. Start capture, open Pokémon GO or Practice in portrait, tap “Set ball”, then select the ball center. Tap “Auto: off” to arm up to five throws. Auto holds the ball to reveal its ring, then continues the same touch into a swipe after a fresh, stable detection. No stable ring means release and Auto off. Calibrate separately in practice and the game. Leaving the target turns Auto off. Automatic holding requires Android 8.0 or newer.
Adjust swipe duration from 150 to 600 milliseconds
Select the ball center in the lower part of the current encounter.
Ball position set. Tap Auto to arm.
Dry run: would hold ball at (%1$.2f, %2$.2f).
Dry run: would swipe to (%1$.2f, %2$.2f) over %3$d ms.
Capture stopped after 10 minutes without a detection. Tap Start for a new session.

Throw Assistant reads your screen to find throw rings and can send swipes through an accessibility service. Using assistance like this with Pokémon GO may violate the game\u2019s terms of service and risks an account ban. Use it at your own risk, ideally on an alternate account.
Please acknowledge the notice to continue.
Kill switch engaged. Capture stopped and Auto is disabled until you re-enable it.
Kill switch is on. Re-enable it in the app to use Auto.

Auto-throw uses an accessibility service to find the game window and perform throw swipes \u2014 only while Auto is armed. It does not read passwords or messages, and nothing ever leaves your device. You can switch it off at any time in Accessibility settings.
Turn on Throw Assistant gestures in Android Accessibility settings.
Gesture permission is enabled, but the service has not connected. If this persists, switch Throw Assistant gestures off and on in Accessibility settings.
Start screen capture before turning Auto on.
Tap the ball center to finish calibration first.
Open the encounter in portrait, then start a new capture session.
Open Practice or a Pokémon GO encounter before using Set ball or Auto.
Open the encounter in a full-screen window before turning Auto on.
Tap Set ball, select the ball center in this encounter, then turn Auto on.
The game window changed since calibration. Tap Set ball to recalibrate.
Wait for the previous gesture to finish before calibrating or arming again.
Automatic holding requires Android 8.0 or newer. Overlay guidance and manual Practice still work.
No stable ring appeared while holding the ball. Auto is off. Check the ball position and capture alignment before trying again.

For ring-detection debugging: saves a numeric-only stats log on this device while capture runs \u2014 analysis time, candidate counts, rejection reasons, and the ring-radius series. No frames or screenshots are ever stored. Turning this off deletes all saved logs.
Session telemetry off. Saved logs deleted.
Timing: too early — the ring will still be wide when the ball lands
Timing: too late — the window closed or the ring reset
